Business purpose

Designed for weekly demand-change control.

The dashboard converts schedule movement into a common management language so buyers and supply-chain teams can see what changed, where the risk sits, and what deserves attention first.

↔

Demand movement

Classifies weekly changes into Pull, Push, No Change, New Add and Remove, with status mix and detailed timing by cutoff date.

△

Shortage exposure

Highlights material shortages by purchasing group, supplier and monthly demand horizon using a red action matrix.

◎

Inventory health

Tracks ROP coverage over time and separates stock that meets ROP from items that fall below the required level.

$

Value normalization

Converts mixed-unit demand into a common monetary view so demand movement can be compared across planning horizons.

⌛

Lead-time intelligence

Segments materials by lead-time band, source multiplicity, supplier and product hierarchy to expose sourcing constraints.

🔎

Spot-buy readiness

Surfaces item and MPN context with shortcuts to Findchips, TrustedParts and Octopart for long-lead or constrained components.

Demand & Supply Change Weekly · 14,425 LD parts · 183 suppliers
Monitor

Separate demand signals from supply response.

The Demand & Supply page brings weekly demand movement and supply movement into the same management view. This makes it easier to see whether material availability is keeping pace with planning changes instead of reviewing demand and supply in isolation.

✓Weekly demand-change trend with Pull and Push direction.
✓Supply trend shown beside item-level stock and supply detail.
✓Shortage overview by monthly demand period and cutoff date.
Material Shortage · 9,383 LD parts shown in shortage scope
Prioritize

Make shortage timing visible at material level.

Instead of a single shortage count, the report shows where the shortage occurs across future demand months and links it to purchasing group, supplier and material identifiers. The red matrix provides an immediate visual signal for months requiring follow-up.

Control inventory

Track ROP health as a trend, not a one-time check.

The ROP page shows both the distribution of parts covered by ROP logic and whether stock actually meets the ROP threshold. The latest snapshot shows 78.86% meeting ROP and 21.14% below ROP, with item-level history for follow-up.

Compare demand changes in dollars across time horizons.

The value view translates heterogeneous demand quantities into a common monetary basis, then compares the current and previous cutoffs across Backlog, 0–3 months, 3–6 months, 6–12 months and beyond 12 months.

Leadtime Masterlist · Lead-time bands, source count and market-search shortcuts
Source smarter

Connect lead-time risk to alternate-source discovery.

The Leadtime Masterlist groups materials into lead-time bands and distinguishes single-source from multiple-source items. It also carries MPN, manufacturer, product hierarchy and material description context to support faster sourcing decisions.

Methodology

A simple status language for schedule movement.

The business logic page in the source report defines the five status categories used throughout the dashboard and the percentage calculation applied to each category.

StatusBusiness definition
Pull InDemand is rescheduled to an earlier week than previously planned.
Push OutDemand is rescheduled to a later week than previously planned.
No ChangeNo change in demand quantity or scheduled week versus the previous week.
New AddA part is newly added this week compared with the previous week.
RemovedA part no longer exists this week compared with the previous week.
Status percentage

Normalize each status against total LD parts

% Pull = Pull / (Pull + Push + No Change + New Add + Remove)

The same denominator logic is applied to Push, No Change, New Add and Remove, creating a consistent weekly status mix.

Executive takeaway

From change detection to action prioritization.

This dashboard is structured to answer four operational questions in sequence: What changed? Where is the shortage? Is inventory protection sufficient? Which long-lead or single-source items need sourcing action?
